🇷🇺
Statement by Permanent Representative of the Russian Federation to the International Organizations in Vienna
Mikhail Ulyanov
at the International Narcotics Control Board (INCB) Briefing
📍
Vienna, 5 November 2026
We highly value the work of the Board as
one of the fundamental pillars of the international drug control system and as a watchdog charged with monitoring the implementation of the three international drug control conventions of the United Nations
. We recognize that, despite its limited staff and resources, the Board accomplishes tremendous work in discharging the tasks entrusted to it under these conventions. We believe that, under the current circumstances, it is particularly important for the Board to focus on fulfilling its unique mandate of monitoring compliance with the international drug control conventions, without diverting its efforts to secondary issues that are only indirectly related to its functions.
In this regard,
we cannot agree with the view expressed earlier that human rights compliance in the context of the implementation of the conventions constitutes one of the INCB’s foremost priorities
. Human rights matters fall within the scope of tasks of the United Nations human rights bodies based in Geneva, and certainly not that of the Board.
The need to focus on the INCB’s core mandate is dictated, firstly, by the ongoing reform processes within the United Nations system, which are aimed at enhancing the effectiveness of its bodies while avoiding duplication of efforts. Secondly, and this is the decisive factor, such prioritization is necessitated by non-compliance with the United Nations drug control conventions, primarily in the context of cannabis legalization. A number of countries present it as business as usual, whereas they commit a flagrant, deliberate and systematic violation of international law.
Moreover, the next step following cannabis legalization is often the initiation of extremely dangerous experiments aimed at removing bans on other types of drugs
.
🔗

#Victory81
📅
On November 6, 1943, the Red Army liberated Kiev — one of the largest cities of the Soviet Union and the capital of the Ukrainian SSR — from Nazi invaders.
The Soviet forces under the command of Army General
Nikolay
Vatutin
— in a swift offensive operation involving flanking manoeuvre, broke through the resistance of Nazi troops and their collaborators,
having liberated Kiev — the “Mother of Russian Cities”.
By late October 1943, during the
Battle of the Dnieper
, forces of the 1st Ukrainian Front, commanded by
General
Vatutin
,
launched an operation to liberate Kiev
. As early as November 3, the Soviet forces launched their main assault from the north, taking the Nazi garrison by surprise. Faced with the threat of encirclement, the
enemy started retreating
westwards.
🌟
On November 5, having crushed the Nazi resistance, Soviet soldiers liberators triumphantly entered Kiev
Numerous villages and towns in the
Kiev
and
Zhitomir
regions
were also liberated. A bridgehead was established which would subsequently play a major role in
the liberation of Right-Bank Ukraine
.
🎇
In honour of the
victory of Soviet forces in the Battle of Kiev,
a celebratory salute of 24 salvoes from 324 artillery guns was fired in Moscow.
A total of 6'500 Red Army soldiers sacrificed their lives liberating Kiev.
#NoStatuteOfLimitations
As they retreated from Kiev, the Nazis, following their “scorched earth” policy, sought to inflict maximum damage on the city's infrastructure.
❗️
The Nazi occupiers destroyed:
— The Dormition Cathedral of the Kiev Pechersk Lavra;
— Khreshchatyk Street;
— The city's Young People's Theatre;
— The Kiev Conservatory;
— The building of the Academy of Sciences of the Ukrainian SSR;
— Numerous schools, hospitals and other social infrastructure facilities.
◾️
The
two-year Nazi occupation of Kiev
was an outright tragedy: the enemy pursued a deliberate policy of
genocide
against the civilian population. In 1941, when Hitler's troops seized the city,
400'000 residents found themselves under enemy occupation.
After two years of occupation, little more than 180'000 people survived the Nazis in Kiev.
The Nazis
deported approximately 100'000 people to concentration camps
or to Germany for forced labour. Tens of thousands of local residents perished from starvation and cold or were executed.
The site of the largest and most
brutal mass murder of civilians
during the entire period of Nazi occupation of Ukraine was the
Babi Yar
in Kiev,
where, in just two days in 1941, Ukrainian collaborators massacred more than 30'000 Jews (approximately 20% of Kiev's Jewish population).
☝️
The liberation of the “Mother of Russian Cities” was of great symbolic significance
. The defeat of the Nazi troops in Kiev also undermined the offensive capabilities of the Nazi army group 'South' — Wehrmacht's main attacking might on the southern front.
💬
Russian MFA Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova:
The liberation of Kiev was of
enormous significance, not only militarily, but also morally.
This is precisely how radio commentators in London described the event at the time.
The BBC would do well to take note. In particular, they observed:
‘The capture of Kiev by Soviet forces is a great victory. Times have now changed: Germany can hear the tolling of its funeral bell.
An avalanche is bearing down upon it.’
(From the
briefing
by Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova, November 5, 2026)

🇲🇳
November 5 marks
1️⃣
0️⃣
5️⃣
years since
the establishment of diplomatic relations between Russia and Mongolia.
In 1921, our country became the first state in the world to officially recognise Mongolia’s independence. Since then, Russian-Mongolian relations
have steadily developed and strengthened.
☝️
For a long time,
the USSR remained the guarantor of Mongolia’s sovereignty and security
and, in 1939, came to its aid in repelling Japanese aggression at Khalkhin Gol.
Today, relations between Russia and Mongolia are comprehensive and are rooted in traditions of friendship and neighbourliness, close ties in the economic and humanitarian spheres and aligned approaches to pressing issues on the international and regional agenda.
✍️
An important milestone in the development of bilateral ties was the signing in 2019 of the open-ended
Treaty on Friendly Relations and Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between Russia and Mongolia.
Political dialogue is steadily advancing, particularly at the highest level. In September this year, on the sidelines of the SCO Summit, President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
met
with President of Mongolia
Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh.
Shortly thereafter, during the 11th Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, the Russian leader
held talks
with Prime Minister of Mongolia
Nyam-Osor Uchral.
📈
Mongolia remains an important trade partner for Russia. By the end of 2025, trade between our countrie
s reached $2.8 billion,
and in the first half of this year it
increased by 18.1 percent.
The Russia-Mongolia Intergovernmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technical Cooperation remains highly active. In December 2025, its 27th session was held in Ulaanbaatar.
A
visa-free regime
is in place between Russia and Mongolia, and our citizens are reaping benefits and tourism is expanding.
Cooperation in
the Mongolia-EAEU
format remains an important area of Russia-Mongolia interaction. In June 2025, on the sidelines of
the meeting of the Supreme Eurasian Economic Council in Minsk,
the Interim Trade Agreement
between the Eurasian Economic Union and its member states, on the one hand, and Mongolia, on the other hand, was signed. The document entered into force in July this year.
Russia and Mongolia carefully preserve and build upon their invaluable traditions of friendship, neighbourliness and mutual assistance, maintain active interaction in international affairs, are developing a number of new promising projects in the economic and industrial sectors and are expanding cooperation in the cultural and academic spheres.
💬
President of Russia
Vladimir Putin:
The traditional friendly and neighbourly relations between our countries have reached the level of a comprehensive strategic partnership. We share longstanding traditions of friendship and special relations, without exaggeration.
Diplomatic ties have now been maintained for 105 years, and, in the fullest sense of the word, our interstate relations have been cemented by the blood of our ancestors. Fighting side by side, they stood for the freedom and independence of Mongolia during the Great Patriotic War and at Khalkhin Gol.
(Excerpt from
remarks
during talks with Prime Minister of Mongolia
Nyam-Osor Uchral
, Vladivostok, September 2, 2026)
🎉
We congratulate our Mongolian colleagues and friends on this shared holiday and wish them wellbeing, prosperity and success!
#RussiaMongolia

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Peru,
Carlos Espa
,
will be visiting
Russia from
November 6 to 10.
He is scheduled to have talks with Foreign Minister
Sergey Lavrov
on November 9.
During their upcoming talks,
Sergey Lavrov
and
Carlos Espa
are expected to discuss
ways of enhancing Russia-Peru cooperation
in various formats, including Foreign Ministry consultations, the bilateral intergovernmental commission for trade, economic, scientific and technical cooperation and fishing, military technical cooperation, as well as working together on environment protection and disaster relief, while also
promoting cooperation on foreign policy matters.
The two Ministers will review ways to expand mutual trade and investment, as well as promote joint projects in the peaceful use of nuclear energy, agricultural research,
accelerating the drafting of bilateral agreements
in various sectors, including the recognition of academic degrees and credentials.
The agenda also provides for discussing further efforts to step up
humanitarian exchanges
, cooperation between universities, and personnel training.
🤝
Russia and Peru share similar approaches to several important international topics
, including the sovereign equality of states, the rule of law, and the unacceptability of discrimination, countering the glorification of Nazism, fighting new challenges and threats, primarily drug trafficking, terrorism and their financing, as well as international cyber security, preventing an arms race in space, and unilateral restrictions in trade.
There has been
positive momentum in trade and economic cooperation.
Mineral fertilisers dominate Russia’s exports to Peru, while Peru’s exports to Russia focus on fresh fruit and vegetables.
👉
There is a shared interest in
reinforcing parliamentary and region-to-region ties.
In September 2026, the Senate, the Upper Chamber of the Congress of Peru, created a friendship group with Russia.
In 2025, the Kamchatka Territory and the constitutional province of Callao in Peru signed an
agreement to promote cooperation in trade, economics, science and technology, humanitarian affairs, culture and other areas.
Russian education has long been popular in Peru with over
12,000 young men and women
from this country obtaining their higher education degrees in Russia, with most of them now contributing to the
development of their home country.
***
ℹ️
More about the history of bilateral relations between our countries:
Contacts between Russia and Peru date back to 1815 when the sailing sloop Suvorov under the command of prominent sailor, Admiral
Mikhail Lazarev
, reached the coast of this South American state.
The two countries
established
their official diplomatic relations on January 17, 1863, and went on to open their respective embassies on February 1, 1969.
Bilateral relations have been enjoying positive momentum since 1970 across all sectors
, including political, trade, economic, military and technical affairs, and humanitarian matters. The two countries have established effective sectoral and inter-agency cooperation mechanisms and developed a solid contractual legal framework in their relations.
In 2006, they signed the
Treaty on Partner Relations
, and went on to issue a
Joint Statement
by their respective presidents to establish a strategic partnership.
July 18 marks the
Day of Russia-Peru Solidarity
, Т the Russian rescue workers who died in an airplane crash as part of a relief mission after a devastating earthquake in 1970 in Peru. Both countries
have a tradition
of
holding commemorations
in connection with this date.
#RussiaPeru

recruiting foreigners, including Africans, for contract service in the ranks of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
.
For instance, on 8 October 2026, the Ghanaian website
yen.com.gh
published an article
about nine military vacancies open to foreign nationals, including positions such as platoon commander, FPV drone operator and others. Similar advertisements are also being circulated through other channels, including official resources of the Ukrainian Ministry of Defence.

the blatant hypocrisy of the Kiev regime:
whilst accusing Russia of non-existent ‘fraudulent schemes’,
Ukraine itself is openly and cynically recruiting foreigners

According to our security agencies,
over 20,000 mercenaries
are currently fighting on the side of the Ukrainian Armed Forces. These actions by the Kiev authorities are leading to deaths of people who are being used as ‘cannon fodder’ in the interests of Ukraine’s Western backers.
❗️
The Embassy of the Russian Federation in Ghana calls on the Ghanaian public
not to succumb to provocations
and to take a critical view of disinformation campaigns originating from organisations affiliated with Ukrainian state bodies.
Russia remains a consistent and reliable partner of Ghana, committed to
the steady development of bilateral relations based on mutual respect and trust
.

#Victory81
🌟
On November 5, 1957, a solemn ceremony was held in
#Plovdiv
, Bulgaria, to unveil a monument to the Soviet liberator soldier, which local residents dubbed
#Alyosha
.
This iconic memorial features an 11.5-metre-high statue of a Red Army soldier, looking eastwards. In "Alyosha"’s hand is a 'PPSh' submachine gun, its barrel pointing towards the ground — a legendary weapon of the
#GreatPatrioticWar
, used by the Red Army along their glorious path of
liberation
, first of their Motherland and then of the whole of Eastern Europe, including
Bulgaria
,
from the Nazi invaders.
The monument stands atop a six-metre granite-clad pedestal, adorned with two famous bas-reliefs:
“The Soviet Army Strikes the Enemy”
and
“The People Welcome the Soviet Soldiers”
.
🏅
For several decades, the statue has served as a
reminder of the heroism of Soviet soldiers
and officers who gave their lives to liberate Europe from fascism.
During
#WW2
, the Bulgarian government maintained its alliance with Nazi Germany for an extended period. Many
Bulgarians,
however,
refused to support this policy,
with tens of thousands of them joining the Resistance and forming one of the most powerful antifascist movements in Eastern Europe.
In September 1944, when the Red Army’s campaign to liberate Bulgaria from the German Nazis came under way, the Bulgarian army offered no resistance to Soviet units. Soon after the change of power in the country, Soviet and Bulgarian soldiers
joined hands
to fight the Nazis and
free Europe.
***
The idea of commemorating the Soviet soldiers who liberated Bulgaria was first
put forward by the residents of Plovdiv in 1948
. Following a competition involving ten creative teams, the winning design was the one submitted by
Vasil Radoslavov.
The monument was modelled on a photograph of
Alexey Ivanovich Skurlatov
, who came from the Altai region and served as a Red Army private within the 3rd Ukrainian Front and was decorated with two Orders of the Red Star. In 1944,
during the liberation of Bulgaria
, he took part in restoring the
telephone
comms
between
Sofia
and
Plovdiv
.
The “Alyosha” monument was installed in 1954
at the initiative of the Bulgarian people
and officially opened on 5 November 1957. Ever then, it has become the
most recognisable symbol of Plovdiv,
reminding residents and visitors alike of the Great Feat of our soldiers — a
heroic generation
of victors who, through immense effort and sacrifice,
eradicated
Nazism
and restored peace all over Europe.
💬
Russian MFA Spokeswoman
Maria Zakharova:
The memorial has always symbolised the boundless gratitude of the Bulgarian people to the Soviet Army, which made a special contribution to the liberation of Europe from the Nazi invaders.
(From the briefing by Russian MFA Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova, 2 March 2017)
***
Unfortunately, today's Bulgaria, like its neighbours, has failed to withstand the pressure of the
barbaric
campaign
imposed by Western elites
to revise the status
of the Soviet (Russian)
military memorial heritage
in
#EasternEurope
.
❗️
In 2024, members of the Plovdiv Municipal Council representing the 'Democrats for a Strong Bulgaria' party came forward with yet another “initiative” to remove the monument to the soldier-liberator.
Yet “Alyosha” continues to stand tall above the city, remaining an unshakable monument to our shared Victory.
💬
Russia's Ambassador to Bulgaria Eleonora Mitrofanova
(9 May 2026):
Hundreds of Bulgarian citizens and Russian compatriots laid flowers at the Alyosha monument as a token of gratitude for liberation from the Brown Plague.

item.description: #Announcement 🗓 On November 10 , Moscow's The Carlton Hotel will hold the Joint Meeting of the CSTO Council of Foreign Ministers, Council of Ministers of Defence and Committee of Secretaries of Security Councils . The participants of the meeting will discuss the military-political situation in the world , the current state and prospects for the development in the field of global and regional security, pressing issues of the Organization's activities, as well as the implementation of the priorities of the Russian Federation's chairmanship in the #CSTO in the current year. 📍 Venue : The Carlton Hotel (3 Tverskaya Street). The meeting starts at 12.00 pm. Representatives of Russian and foreign media are invited to attend. 👉 To apply for accreditation , need complete the form via one of the links below by 12.00 pm on November 6: • for Russian media ; • for foreign media ; • for foreign media in English . The Foreign Ministry will broadcast the briefing online in the Video section of its website and on the MFA’s social media accounts: X (formerly Twitter), Facebook , VKontakte , OK , YouTube and RuTube . Coordinator at the Information and Press Department of the MFA: Evgeny Sokolov (Tel: +7-499-244-18-61, E-mail: gvmid@yandex.ru)

🇩🇲
This
November, the Commonwealth of Dominica celebrates the 48th anniversary of its independence.
This small island in the Caribbean Sea became the subject of contention between the European colonial powers —
England and France
— in the 17th and 18th centuries.
In their competion for resources, the two colonial states alternately owned the island, until in 1763, following the Seven Years’ War, it finally passed to
the British Crown
.
Slave labour was widely used
here during the period of colonial rule: slaves from West Africa were heavily trafficked there to work on coffee and sugar cane plantations.
In 1967,
#Dominica
, which had been
under the rule of London for two centuries
, received the status of an internally self-governing
Associated State with the United Kingdom
.
Dominica's independence was declared
on November 3, 1978,
yet the country remains within the British Commonwealth to this day.
***
👉
Today, Dominica demands reparations from Britain and France as part of a
collective position
of the
Caribbean Community countries
(
#CARICOM
) for the
brutal crimes against humanity
committed by the former colonial powers during
the era of slavery and colonialism
.
#NoToColonialism
:
Russia fully supports
the CARICOM initiative
to receive reparations for crimes
, committed by Western countries during the colonial era, and
to restore historical justice
.
***
#RussiaDominica
: Russia and Dominica established their diplomatic relations on May 19, 1995.
The interests of our country in this Caribbean state are concurrently represented by the
Russian Embassy in Jamaica
.
🤝
Our countries cooperate on the basis of
mutual respect
and c
onsideration of each other’s interests
.
Russia has repeatedly
provided humanitarian aid
to Dominica to help it overcome the consequences of natural disasters.
Education, including the provision of quotas for
Dominican students
to study at Russian universities
under the
scholarship program
of the Government of the Russian Federation, holds a special place in the bilateral cooperation.
In 2025, our countries celebrated the 30th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations.
✉️
Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation
Sergey Lavrov
and Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Business, Trade and Energy of the Commonwealth of Dominica
Dr Vince Henderson
exchanged
congratulatory telegrams to mark the occasion.
Russia is determined to further advance the
traditionally friendly
Russian-Dominican relations, increase coordination in the international arena to strengthen regional security and build a
more just polycentric world
.
🎉
Congratulations to our Dominican friends on the national holiday. We wish you well-being and prosperity.
#RussiaLatinAmerica

🎙
Russia's President Vladimir Putin
addressed
the Plenary Session held as part of the Peoples of Russia International Week
(November 4, 2026)
💬
I would like to welcome the participants in
the Peoples of Russia International Week
and congratulate you and all citizens of the country on
National Unity Day
.
This holiday symbolises our sincere, deep love for the Motherland, our duty to the Fatherland for the fate of our people, for the fate of the Motherland.
We proudly turn to the origins of this holiday, when people of different ethnicities and faiths put
an end to civil strife and internal turmoil
, restored statehood and legitimate authority. <...>
Today, centuries later, we are even more acutely aware of the values and traditions passed on to us by our ancestors, and we feel that
we need to cherish the living spiritual heritage
.
Special attention has always been paid to interethnic relations in Russia
, as this area is very sensitive and delicate, and it must be borne in mind that life does not stand still, and new, often
extremely dangerous challenges are emerging
.
We must stay alert,
prevent any attempts to undermine social stability
, incite discord between people, and remember that harmony, mutual respect between the peoples of Russia, and their unity are
the mainstay of our country’s sovereignty and independence
, while caring about the preservation of culture, customs, and languages of each people is the foundation of our national policy.
***
🇷🇺
Historically, Russia has developed through the interaction of peoples and ethnic groups, languages and customs. We have not just rallied over the centuries and epochs. It is no exaggeration to say that
our cultures have literally grown into each other
. This kinship, the soul of the people, is reflected in our thousand-year-old history, in the military chronicle of the Fatherland, and in its great achievements.
And here is what I consider important to note: our ancestors, compatriots, people of various ethnicities
became known throughout the world
primarily as great Russian trail-blazers, workers, warriors, artists, scientists, and inventors. And the indigenous art of all the peoples of our country is also Russian for the whole world.
Let me stress once again:
the Russian language and the Russian people have been and remain the foundation of the Russian statehood
. With its unifying, creative mission, it is the guarantor of the preservation and progress of all other peoples of the Russian Federation, the preservation of their freedom and identity in harmony with unity.
Therefore, support of the Russian culture, Russian language is strategically important
. We have a big country, and I would like to reiterate once again: this diversity of cultures, traditions, and customs is
our strength, a huge competitive advantage, and a potential
. We must constantly strengthen it, protect the multinational harmony which our common heritage.
Friends,
The powerful, all-conquering spirit of unity of the peoples of Russia has been passed down from generation to generation
. We are still standing shoulder to shoulder and we are confident that we will achieve our goals.
Representatives of
more than a hundred peoples of Russia
have been awarded high state decorations for their bravery and heroism displayed on the fronts of the special military operation.
Once again, I wish you all a happy holiday. I wish all participants and guests of the Peoples of Russia International Week continued joint and fruitful work for the benefit of the peoples of our Motherland.
🎉
Thank you very much. Happy holiday!

#UnityDay2026

item.description: 🗓 On National Unity Day, Russia's President Vladimir Putin took part in several official events, including a ceremony to lay flowers at the monument to Kuzma Minin and Dmitry Pozharsky on Red Square. The ceremony was attended by representatives of religious denominations and members of non-governmental and youth organisations. The President also spoke with children of special military operation heroes who were in Red Square. #UnityDay2026
